title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 36 (Punishment for fraudulently inducing persons to invest money)

content.overview: Section 36 provides that any person who, either knowingly or recklessly, makes any statement, promise or forecast which is false, deceptive or misleading, or deliberately conceals any material facts, to induce another person to enter into, or to offer to enter into, (a) any agreement for, or with a view to, acquiring, disposing of, subscribing for, or underwriting securities; or (b) any agreement the purpose or pretended purpose of which is to secure a profit to any of the parties from the yield of securities or by reference to fluctuations in the value of securities; or (c) any agreement for, or with a view to, obtaining credit facilities from any bank or financial institution, shall be liable for action under section 447.
content.glance: Knowing or reckless false/deceptive/misleading statement, promise or forecast, or deliberate concealment of material facts, to induce specified securities or credit agreements → liability under s. 447.
content.study: Any person who, either knowingly or recklessly, makes any statement, promise or forecast which is false, deceptive or misleading, or deliberately conceals any material facts, to induce another person to enter into, or to offer to enter into—(a) any agreement for, or with a view to, acquiring, disposing of, subscribing for, or underwriting securities; or (b) any agreement, the purpose or the pretended purpose of which is to secure a profit to any of the parties from the yield of securities or by reference to fluctuations in the value of securities; or (c) any agreement for, or with a view to, obtaining credit facilities from any bank or financial institution, shall be liable for action under section 447. Current-law framing: identify the statement/promise/forecast or concealment; prove the knowing or reckless (or deliberate) mental element; prove the inducement purpose; confirm the target agreement falls within clauses (a)–(c); then apply section 447.

sections.heading: Prohibited conduct
sections.body: Making any statement, promise or forecast which is false, deceptive or misleading, or deliberately concealing any material facts.

sections.heading: Mental element
sections.body: Knowing or reckless as to the statement, promise or forecast; deliberate as to concealment of material facts.

sections.heading: Inducement targets (a)–(c)
sections.body: (a) agreement for or with a view to acquiring, disposing of, subscribing for or underwriting securities; (b) agreement whose purpose or pretended purpose is to secure a profit from the yield of securities or by reference to fluctuations in their value; (c) agreement for or with a view to obtaining credit facilities from any bank or financial institution.

sections.heading: Consequence
sections.body: Liable for action under section 447 (punishment for fraud).

provisions.title: Punishment for fraudulently inducing persons to invest money

examples.title: False forecast to induce subscription
examples.body: A person knowingly makes a false profit forecast to induce another to subscribe for securities. Section 36 engages liability under section 447.

examples.title: Deliberate concealment for credit facility
examples.body: Material facts are deliberately concealed to induce a bank to grant a credit facility. Section 36(c) applies.

hypotheticals.question: Is section 36 limited to formal prospectuses?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. It targets statements, promises, forecasts and concealment used to induce the specified investment or credit agreements, whether or not contained in a formal prospectus.

distinctions.title: Fraudulent inducement (s. 36) vs prospectus misstatement crime (s. 34)
distinctions.left: Broader inducement conduct (any person; not limited to prospectus authorisation)
distinctions.right: Authorising issue of a prospectus containing untrue or misleading statements

rows.left: Inducement to invest or obtain credit

misconceptions.trap: Section 36 only applies to directors who sign a prospectus.
misconceptions.correction: It applies to any person who knowingly or recklessly makes the prohibited communication or deliberately conceals material facts to induce the specified agreements.

misconceptions.trap: Section 36 is limited to securities agreements and does not cover credit facilities.
misconceptions.correction: Clause (c) expressly covers agreements for obtaining credit facilities from any bank or financial institution.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 36 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the statement, promise, forecast or concealment. II. Prove the mental element (knowing/reckless or deliberate). III. Prove inducement of a clause (a), (b) or (c) agreement. IV. Apply section 447. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Conduct; mental element; target agreement category; section 447 consequence; precise relief.

examTips: State knowing/reckless or deliberate mental element.
